l.i: Qua sensilia sensus ipsos & instrumenta laedat.

main_text.l: ÆTERVM sensilia nec sensus, nec orgona labefactant, nisi mo-dum excedant. Quare grauis so-nus & acutus auditum laedit, vt & visum colores splendidissimi & obscurissimi, odoratum grauissimi & teterrimi odores, quoniam sensus velut quaedam commoderatio est. Quamobrem sensilium ea, quae commoderata sunt sensus delectant. Contraria vero eos labefactant. Proinde tactui simplex calidum, aut frigidum, aut aliud tale non iucundum est & amicum, sed quod ad rationem temperationemque redactum est.

Sensus enim velut ratio est: propterea sensilium ea quae exuperant, aut ipsi moleftiam afferunt, aut tandem eum corrumpunt: quoniam mouentis actio est, sensus vero & instrumenti perpessio. Caeterum rei sensilis actioni, & sensus instrumetique passioni nomen vnum impositum est, vt auditui actu, & sono actu auditio, visui actu & coloris, visio, gustatui gustatio, & tactui tractatio, olfactui olfactio.
Uniâ[?] sensu & intellectu res om-nes noftra anima iudicat & cognofcit, veteres philosophi, praeter Aristotelem, sentire & intelligere

page.notes: The Æ and Q openings are woodcut initials, transcribed joined to their words. "orgona" is printed (probably for "organa"), kept as printed. "Uniâ[?]" at the start of the last paragraph is uncertain: the first letter is a decorative capital and the tilde over the a is unclear. The paragraph break before "Sensus enim" follows a short sentence-end line. The last line ends the page; the text continues on the next page. Long s rendered as f in the print is transcribed as s.
